title: RGB--Event Object Detection Across Operating Frequencies via Reliability-Supervised Routing and Asymmetric-Resolution Fusion

problem.summary: Event cameras record brightness changes with microsecond resolution, so RGB-event detectors can decide between frames, at an operating frequency, the rate of decisions, far above the frame rate.
statements: Event cameras record brightness changes with microsecond resolution, so RGB-event detectors can decide between frames, at an operating frequency, the rate of decisions, far above the frame rate.
As this rate rises, each decision receives a sparser event window, and the reliability of the events relative to the frame varies over the scene and over time.
Existing detectors weight the sensors per sample and encode the frame at the reduced event resolution.

background.summary: The principle of this paper is that the fusion should track, location by location and decision by decision, which sensor is more reliable; robustness across operating frequencies is its measurable instance, as a shorter event window lowers the reliability of the events at a fixed frame.

components: Asymmetric-Resolution Fusion The DSEC frames are registered to the event camera at 640 × 480 pixels, and the detector uses the top 430 rows.

The RGB encoder needs to run only once per frame, yet the resize discards three quarters of the pixels before it sees them, and the loss is largest for small objects, whose detection accuracy depends on the scale at which the encoder sees them [39].

Asymmetric-resolution fusion sets the two resolutions separately and moves the change of resolution from the image to the feature pyramid: the events keep the grid of the base detector, and the frame is encoded at k = 2 times this resolution, its native 640 × 430 on DSEC-Det.

experiments.summary: Between 20 Hz and 180 Hz it loses 3.07 mAP and retains 95.2% of its accuracy, against 78.1% for FlexEvent Global and 89.1% for FlexEvent Balanced, and between 20 Hz and 90 Hz it retains 99.8%.

At 180 Hz, ERA-Det, at 61.34 mAP, is more accurate than FlexEvent Global at 20 Hz, at 60.12 mAP.

limitations.summary: Because the RGB features depend only on the frame, a deployment computes them once per frame and reuses them for all decisions until the next frame arrives.
items: Because the RGB features depend only on the frame, a deployment computes them once per frame and reuses them for all decisions until the next frame arrives.

Reliability-supervised routing realizes it by supervising a fusion weight at every location with targets from two single-modality classifiers, a supervision that earlier fusion methods apply only to whole samples, and asymmetric-resolution fusion gives the frame the evidence that routing relies on by decoupling its resolution from that of the events while every pretrained weight is reused.
ERA-Det is obtained by fine-tuning released weights for only 5,000 iterations on a single GPU.
